findings.title: Owner names logged at info on every grid page
findings.observation: every grid request logs up to 20 owners' full names: personal data in logs, shipped to aggregators.
findings.why: the human asked for exactly this log line, at Q&A.md:15.

findings.title: A page past the end costs a second query
findings.observation: an out-of-range page runs the page and count queries, then again for the last page.
findings.why: happens only on stale or bad pages; serving the last page is Q&A.md:12.

findings.title: A backend failure renders as "No visits found."
findings.observation: catchError substitutes an empty page, so an outage looks like an empty clinic with no retry.
findings.why: the old getVisits swallowed errors into [] the same way; no error page per Q&A.md:12.

findings.title: Paginator vanishes when a page comes back empty
findings.observation: the table, headers and paginator hide together whenever content is empty.
findings.why: content is empty only for an empty clinic; past the end serves the last page (VisitRestController.findGridPageWithinBounds).

findings.title: Sort glue would fail on an empty database
findings.observation: the Then step needs 10 rows but no DB fixture appeared to be declared.
findings.why: refuted; the feature is tagged @fixture:default, which loads the 30-visit seed.

findings.title: Old list tests disabled, not replaced
findings.observation: getAll and getAll_returnsEnrichedFields are @Disabled; nothing covers findGridPage against a database.
findings.why: disabling them is Q&A.md:18; VisitGridTest covers findGridPage on Zonky Postgres.

findings.title: Sorting is case- and accent-blind to linguistic order
findings.observation: the DB collates by code point, so uppercase sorts before lowercase and "Ștefan" after "Wendy".
findings.why: database collation (C.UTF-8) decides; a linguistic collation is a separate follow-up.

findings.title: The v.id tie-breaker has no test
findings.observation: dropping the v.id tie-breaker would keep everything green.
findings.why: refuted; sortsByTheColumnThenByIdForAStablePaging asserts the v.id order and would fail.

findings.title: Acceptance test passes for a client-side sort too
findings.observation: checking only that the first page is ordered also passes if the browser sorts 10 rows itself.
findings.why: Q&A.md:21 fixes this exact check; VisitGridTest pins the server-side sort.

autofixes.title: A huge page overflowed the int offset into a 500
autofixes.observation: page was clamped only to Integer.MAX_VALUE, so page × size overflowed the int offset JPA takes and ?page=2147483647&size=20 threw a 500 instead of serving the last page.
autofixes.fix: cap the page at Integer.MAX_VALUE / size, and clamp the size into [5, 20] before snapping so a huge negative size cannot overflow either.

autofixes.title: navigate() promise left floating
autofixes.observation: router.navigate returns a promise nobody handled; Sonar rates it a BUG and the quality gate fails on it.

autofixes.title: Generic length assertion in the visits page spec
Sort test passed even if sorting ran after the LIMIT
autofixes.observation: each column's test only checked that the 10 rows shown were in order, so a sort applied to the page instead of the table would still pass.
autofixes.fix: each case also asserts the first row is the global extreme of that column.

autofixes.title: Missing space in the Visit type declaration

assumptions.title: The repository selects straight into VisitRowDto
Bad params are corrected, never answered with 400
Owner column sorts by first name, then last name
assumptions.alternative: last name first, the usual directory order
assumptions.why: the column shows "First Last", so this order reads sorted on screen and lets the acceptance test compare the visible text. A clinic may still expect surname order, which keeps it near a coin flip.

assumptions.title: A size equidistant from two allowed sizes snaps down
assumptions.why: "nearest" leaves the tie open; the stream takes the first, smaller size. Nobody types 15, so it barely matters.

assumptions.title: An unreadable page number serves the first page
assumptions.alternative: treat it as past the end and serve the last page
assumptions.why: Q3 names only "past the end"; garbage reads closest to "no page given", which defaults to the first.

assumptions.title: Page, size and sort live in the URL query
assumptions.alternative: component state only, lost on reload
assumptions.why: a reload or Back keeps the front desk's place. It is not asked for, but it is cheap and fits Angular routing.

assumptions.title: The response echoes the sort it actually applied
assumptions.alternative: the client trusts the sort it asked for
assumptions.why: after a fallback the header arrows must show the order actually served; the echo is built only from our own constants.
